dedupe_keys.name: itopf oil tanker spill statistics tanker spills since 1970 by size cause and quantity

description: ITOPF, the International Tanker Owners Pollution Federation, maintains a database of oil spills from tank vessels, including combined carriers, FPSOs and barges, covering accidental spills of persistent and non-persistent oil since 1970 except those caused by acts of war. The statistics page, read on 2026-09-26, says the database records the location and cause, the vessel, the oil type and the amount, with spills sized as small (under 7 tonnes), medium (7 to 700 tonnes) and large (over 700 tonnes); more than 10,000 incidents are held. Sources are the shipping press, vessel owners, insurers and ITOPF's own attendance. The 2025 edition reports three large and three medium spills and about 4,000 tonnes lost in 2025, and figures on spill frequency by decade since 1970, quantities and spills against seaborne trade. The statistics are free to read; ITOPF does not give direct access to the database or release names of individual incidents not already public, and no licence is stated. Caveats: completeness depends on published reports, and small spills are under-recorded in early decades. Simulation uses are frequency and size inputs for hazard exposure and resilience studies of tanker transport. Related records: data-noaa-incidentnews-oil-spills lists US incidents with coordinates.
